_readme: THE single source of truth for which capability tier each agent role earns.
Policy is written in TIER names everywhere else in this repo (CLAUDE.md, agent
prompts, .ai/ docs). Concrete vendor model ids appear ONLY in capability_tiers
below, so a model release is a one-line edit here instead of a corpus-wide sweep.
Role and capability are chosen SEPARATELY: `accountable_for` says what the role
owns, `tier` says how much intelligence the assignment earns.
Regenerate/verify agent frontmatter with: python3 scripts/gen-model-policy.py [--check]
`callsite_overrides` records every place a concrete model is written by hand. A
site is legitimate only if it appears here with a reason; the audit test refuses
any `--model` literal that is neither a role's resolved tier nor a listed override.

most-capable.use_when: Novel design, adversarial review, security reasoning, or root-cause work where a wrong answer is expensive and hard to detect.

balanced.use_when: Bounded judgement against a written standard: scoring, specialist review, refactors, test authoring, orchestration.

fast.use_when: Mechanical or retrieval work with a checkable output: executing an approved ops.json, searching, summarising, formatting.

build-error-resolver.accountable_for: Smallest possible diff that clears a build or type error.

code-reviewer.accountable_for: Adversarial review of an implementation diff; refute, do not approve.

code-simplifier.accountable_for: Clarity and consistency of already-working code, behaviour preserved.

coordinator.accountable_for: Decomposition, file-ownership maps, and handoffs between agents.
coordinator.escalate_when: Blast-radius Tier 3: security surface, schema migrations, >15 ops, or >2 phases.

database-architect.escalate_when: Destructive or non-reversible migrations on live data.

doc-updater.accountable_for: Syncing existing docs and docstrings with code that changed.

documenter.accountable_for: Authoring new reference documentation from source.

explore.accountable_for: Locating files and answering architecture questions, read-only.

gitOps.accountable_for: Branching, committing, pushing, and PR mechanics.

harness-optimizer.accountable_for: Reliability and cost of the local agent harness configuration.

implementer.accountable_for: Executing an approved ops.json through the operations engine. Never edits.

loop-operator.accountable_for: Supervising autonomous loops; pause on stagnation or error spirals.

model-router.accountable_for: Scoring a task and naming the capability tier it earns.

opensource-packager.accountable_for: Generating open-source packaging for an already-sanitized repo.

opensource-sanitizer.accountable_for: PASS/FAIL secret, PII, and internal-reference scan before publication.
opensource-sanitizer.escalate_when: The repo has handled production credentials or customer data.

performance-optimizer.accountable_for: Latency, memory, and throughput analysis and fixes.

planner.accountable_for: Implementation plans plus a machine-executable ops.json.

python-reviewer.accountable_for: Python-specific correctness, typing, and idiom review.

refactor-cleaner.accountable_for: Dead code and duplicate removal, behaviour preserved.

reviewer.accountable_for: Scoring a plan + ops.json against the 90/100 threshold.
reviewer.escalate_when: The plan is multi-phase, changes architecture, or touches a security surface.

security-scanner.accountable_for: Active SAST, CVE, secret, and hardening audit.

silent-failure-hunter.accountable_for: Swallowed errors, bad fallbacks, and missing propagation.

tdd-guide.accountable_for: Enforcing RED/GREEN/REFACTOR order and coverage discipline.

tester.accountable_for: Authoring behavioural tests for existing code.

verifier.accountable_for: Running the gates and scoring against the 80/100 threshold.

web-researcher.accountable_for: The only agent that calls WebSearch/WebFetch; returns a distilled answer.

callsite_overrides._why: Commands ship to user projects, where repo-root scripts/ does not exist (install.sh:203 copies only .claude/operations/scripts/*.py), so an invocation cannot resolve a tier at run time. Rather than leave the literals unguarded, every one is enumerated: the audit test derives the expected value from the table for ordinary sites and demands a reason for the rest. Note: a site is registered only if the literal SURVIVES this change. model-router.md's example was rewritten into a tier lookup instead, so it needs no entry - registering one would have failed the registry-decay test immediately.

sites.reason: Deliberate model DIVERSITY, not a tier choice: the santa-method pairs two reviewers on different models so neither anchors on the other. Resolving both from one tier would defeat the pattern.
